summary: Build practical recovery plans, referral pathways, and reporting tools for post-disaster health settings. Train with Trainingcred.
lede: Health and medical recovery in post-disaster settings requires more than reopening services; it calls for structured assessment, triage, rehabilitation, referral coordination, and continuity planning. This course helps you identify service gaps, prioritize recovery actions, and track progress across clinical and community services. You will practice creating needs assessments, rehabilitation plans, referral pathways, service restoration trackers, and stakeholder situation briefs. The course also shows how to use coordination logs, recovery dashboards, and decision tools to report credible progress despite limited supplies, damaged records, staff fatigue, interrupted transport, and uneven capacity.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to restore essential health services, coordinate rehabilitation, and document recovery progress after a disaster.
prerequisites: Prior experience in health services, emergency response, humanitarian operations, rehabilitation, or public health programming is recommended. A working understanding of disaster response coordination is useful, but you do not need advanced statistics or programming skills. Participants should bring a laptop for template-based exercises, recovery mapping tasks, and digital reporting practice. Familiarity with patient flow, referral systems, service delivery tracking, or health program reporting will help you apply the course content more quickly.
